# skillful

You are working on the skillful CLI. The job is one authored corpus of
skills, commands, and rules; Git for other people's trees; one render per
harness. Only `install` writes live destinations.

The CLI is the product. Nix consumes the same lock and renderer so a project
is Nix-compatible from the first pin. It is not the product story. Do not put
Nix in `--help` or `guides/`.

User-facing orientation lives in `--help` and `guides/`. This file orients
agents in the repo. It is not a second README.

## CLI copy

When a command, invariant, or topic changes, update `--help` and
`skillful skills tree` / `skills show` in the same change. Those surfaces
are the docs. Do not add a parallel handbook.

`--help` orients: purpose, when to use this at all, what must not happen,
grouped commands, then `skills tree` and `<command> --help`. No Nix, no
marketing, no empty-array defaults, no synonym table.

`skills tree` lists exact topic names. `skills show <topic>` loads one
guide. A miss reprints the tree. Guides say what the topic is and is not,
the exact commands, and the next topic. Topic names are CLI names; do not
invent verbs or aliases.

Per-command after-help says when to use the verb, one or two examples, and
the next command. Skip after-help that only repeats the usage line.

# Agent JJ

# skillful **Pin, compose and override agent skills across every coding agent and machine you use.** Skillful is a skills manager for people who run several coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Pi) on more than one machine. One file says where your skills come from, which agents get them and what each machine selects. Skillful locks other people's skills to an exact revision, applies your changes without a fork, and writes each agent's native layout. ```text skillful 2 local ./skills ./commands rules ./rules/global_agents.md use github:vercel-labs/agent-browser/skills@main { agent-browser } agent-browser.description = "Drive a real browser from the terminal. Use for any task on a website." agent-browser.body.append on pi = "\nRun long browser sessions through the process tool.\n" agent-browser.body.replace "npm i -g agent-browser" with "bun add -g agent-browser" agents claude codex pi cursor skip agent-browser on cursor "Cursor has its own browser" machine work-mac machine laptop skip agent-browser ``` That is a whole project's `skill.mod`: your own skills, one upstream skill with three changes, four agents and two machines. On `work-mac` it installs: ```console $ skillful install work-mac --dry-run Would install into /Users/you: 8 add, 0 change, 0 delete add .agents/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md add .claude/CLAUDE.md add .claude/skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md add .claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md add .codex/AGENTS.md add .codex/skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md add .pi/agent/AGENTS.md add .pi/agent/skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md ``` Your own `release-notes` skill is written once to `.agents/skills`, which Codex, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode and Pi all read, and once for Claude Code. `agent-browser` differs between agents, so each agent that gets it has its own copy, and Cursor has none. On `laptop` it is left out altogether. Your rules land in each agent's own rules file, such as `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. ## Why skillful - **Pinned.** `skill.lock` records the exact revision of every upstream source and a hash of the whole fetched tree. Nothing moves until you run `skillful update`. - **Yours without a fork.** Change an upstream skill's description or instructions from `skill.mod`, and hear about it when upstream changes what you replaced. - **One source, every agent.** Each agent gets the folders, front matter and command files it expects. No agent gets the same skill twice. - **Per machine.** Name each machine and what it skips. The same repository installs the right set everywhere. A single agent on a single machine doesn't need this. Plain files are enough. ## Install Skillful builds to one standalone binary with [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4.4 or later. The binary needs Git and `tar` at runtime, and nothing else. ```sh git clone https://github.com/builtwithtofu/skillful cd skillful bun install --frozen-lockfile bun run build ./dist/skillful --help ``` Put `dist/skillful` on your `PATH`. ## Start Try a local-only project without editing any files: ```sh skillful init --dir ./example-agent cd ./example-agent skillful render skillful install example --dry-run ``` `init` writes the simplest `skill.mod`, which installs as it is: ```text skillful 2 local ./skills ./commands rules ./rules/global_agents.md agents claude codex cursor grok opencode pi machine example ``` `skillful install example` installs that machine. Name a machine after a computer's short hostname (`hostname -s`, in lowercase) and plain `skillful install` picks it there. When no machine matches, it stops and lists the ones you declared. To build the project shown above instead, start in a separate directory. A project is a directory holding `skill.mod`, your own skills, commands and rules, and the `skill.lock` that skillful writes. ```sh mkdir -p agent/skills/release-notes agent/commands agent/rules cd agent echo "Keep replies short." > rules/global_agents.md ``` Write one skill of your own in `skills/release-notes/SKILL.md`: ```markdown --- name: release-notes description: Write release notes from the commits since the last tag. Use when cutting a release. --- # Release notes List what changed for users, newest first. Leave out refactors and chores. ``` Save the file at the top of this page as `skill.mod`, then pin, check and install: ```sh skillful update # resolve each `use` and write skill.lock skillful check # validate the project skillful install work-mac --dry-run # show what would be written skillful install work-mac # write it ``` Only `install` writes to your agents' folders. It refuses to overwrite files it doesn't own. Commit `skill.mod` and `skill.lock`. On your next machine: ```sh skillful fetch # download exactly what the lock names skillful install laptop # or `skillful install`, if its hostname is laptop ``` ## Pin `use { skills }` takes the named skills from a `github:`, `git:` or `path:` source. `skillful update` writes one line per source to `skill.lock`: the ref, the commit it resolved to, and a hash of the fetched tree. - The hash covers every file in the tree, so a skill's scripts, references and assets are verified along with its `SKILL.md`. This matters most for skills that ship scripts your agent will run. - Pins move only when you run `skillful update`, or `skillful update github:vercel-labs/agent-browser/skills@main` for one source. - `skillful fetch` fails with a hash mismatch if the tree at a pinned revision is not the one you locked. - `check`, `render` and `install` never touch the network. Add another source with `skillful add`: ```sh skillful add github:angular/skills@main --only angular-developer ``` ## Override Change any selected skill from `skill.mod`. The upstream repository stays untouched and your changes are reapplied on every update. ```text agent-browser.description = "Drive a real browser from the terminal. Use for any task on a website." agent-browser.body.append on pi = "\nRun long browser sessions through the process tool.\n" agent-browser.body.replace "npm i -g agent-browser" with "bun add -g agent-browser" ``` - `. = value` replaces a front-matter field, and `.append` adds to it. - `.body = value` replaces the instructions, `.body.append` adds to them, and `.body.replace A with B` swaps one exact passage. - A value is a quoted string, or a path such as `./overlays/browser.md`. - `on ` limits an override to one agent. A `.body.replace` whose passage isn't found exactly once stops the render and names the skill and the locked revision. After upstream changes a field or body you replaced with `=`, `skillful check` warns and names it, so you can look at the new text before your override hides it. ## Agents and machines ```text agents claude codex pi cursor skip agent-browser on cursor "Cursor has its own browser" machine work-mac machine laptop skip agent-browser ``` - `agents` lists the agents to render for. Every skill goes to every agent. - `skip on "reason"` keeps skills from some agents. - `machine ` declares a machine, and `skip` on its line removes skills there only. Everything about where things install lives in `skill.mod` too. The defaults cover the common case, and three more lines cover the rest: ```text only release-notes on claude codex "Releases are cut from these two" harness pi { skills .pi/work/skills } machine studio { harness claude { skills .claude-work/skills } skip agent-browser } ``` - `only on "reason"` gives skills to the named agents and no others. - `harness { skills commands rules }` changes where an agent's files go, or defines an agent skillful doesn't know. Anything you leave out keeps its default. Add `reads-shared` for a new agent that reads `.agents/skills`. - A `machine` takes braces only when it has its own `harness`, which wins over the top-level one on that machine. ```sh skillful list skills # which agents get each skill skillful setup show laptop # what one machine installs, and where skillful render laptop # build the tree under ./rendered without installing ``` ## Migrate from skillful 1 Files that start `skillful 1` keep working. To move one to skillful 2: ```sh skillful migrate skillful render --dry-run ``` `migrate` rewrites `skill.mod` and local body fences in place and keeps your pins. It stops without writing if a setting can't be translated without changing what renders. The same project in each form, below its root lines:
skillful 1skillful 2
```text require github:vercel-labs/agent-browser/skills@main as agent-browser ( only agent-browser ) harness claude ( ) harness codex ( ) harness cursor ( omit-skill agent-browser "Cursor has its own browser" ) harness pi ( ) setup laptop ( omit-skill agent-browser "Not used on the laptop." claude codex pi cursor ) setup work-mac ( claude codex pi cursor ) ``` ```text use github:vercel-labs/agent-browser/skills@main { agent-browser } agents claude codex cursor pi skip agent-browser on cursor "Cursor has its own browser" // "agent-browser": "Not used on the laptop." machine laptop skip agent-browser machine work-mac ```
## Learn more The CLI carries its own documentation. ```sh skillful --help # what skillful is for, and every command skillful skills tree # the list of guides skillful skills show mod # one guide: everything skill.mod accepts skillful --help # flags and examples for one command ``` ## Use with Nix Nix can build the same project from the same lock. It reads `skill.lock`, fetches those exact pins with `fetchTree`, and runs `skillful render` with no network and no import-from-derivation. The CLI is `inputs.skillful.packages.${system}.skillful`. ```nix project = inputs.skillful.lib.mkProject { inherit pkgs; source = self; projectDir = "agent"; dependencyOverrides.shared = inputs.shared-skills; extraRoots.skills = [ { origin = "workstation"; source = ./host-skills; } ]; }; packages.${system}.default = project.rendered; checks.${system} = project.checks; pi = project.forHarness "pi"; # pi = { paths; skills; commands; rules; } laptop = project.forSetup "laptop"; # laptop = { name; root; selection; rendered; harnesses; files; } ``` `forSetup` takes a skillful 2 `machine` name or a skillful 1 `setup` name and builds the same layout as `skillful install`, shared skills folder included. Home Manager can consume its `files` map directly: ```nix home.file = pkgs.lib.mapAttrs (_: file: { inherit (file) source recursive; }) laptop.files; ``` - `project.rendered` is the complete render, and `project.forHarness` is one agent's view. Deploy from `files`; `rendered` is a build tree, not a destination map. - `source` is the flake (`self`) or another flake input, and `projectDir` is the directory holding `skill.mod`. `path:../shared/skills` dependencies can reach sibling trees in the same source. Relative working-tree paths are rejected. - `dependencyOverrides` substitute a declared, locked remote while rendering and never replace its lock entry. `extraRoots` add host content without editing `skill.mod`. - Pins still move only through `skillful update`. `nix flake update` does not move them. ## Development ```sh bun install --frozen-lockfile bun test cli bun run typecheck nix flake check path:. ``` ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

# A skillful project

From this directory, render the example and preview where it would install:

```sh
skillful render
skillful install example --dry-run
```

Edit `skill.mod` and the files under `skills/`, `commands/`, and `rules/` to make
this project your own. Run `skillful skills show mod` for the manifest guide.

# author

Write one `SKILL.md`. The frontmatter `name` and `description` are the load gate.
The body says how and when to use the skill — not a restatement of the files beside it.

Not `mod` (that declares the project). Not `render` (that emits harness files).

A skill folder is `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, optional `references/` and scripts. The
model loads a skill when its description matches, and the person can invoke it too.

A command is a saved prompt the person runs by name: `commands/<name>.md`, separate
from any skill. Pi, OpenCode, and Grok receive it as a prompt or command file. Claude,
Codex, and Cursor have no saved prompts, so it becomes a skill only the person can
invoke. A command needs no `SKILL.md`; a skill folder cannot hold a `COMMAND.md`, and a
command cannot share a skill's name. Codex and Cursor require Agent Skill names for
skills and commands: at most 64 lowercase letters, numbers, and single hyphens.

`$@` is the argument placeholder; the renderer translates it per harness. Markup in
code spans and fenced code blocks is shown as written. A render error names the file
and line and tells you how to fix it. For an overridden body, the error names the
skill file and lists the override lines in `skill.mod`.

In skillful 2 skill, command, and rules bodies, put each fence on its own line:

```markdown
<!-- only codex pi -->
These lines go to Codex or Pi.
<!-- end -->
<!-- skip codex pi -->
These lines go to every other agent.
<!-- end -->
```

Fences cannot nest. Selectors are whitespace-separated built-in harness names or
custom names listed in `agents`; any one match is enough. `model:...` and other
`kind:value` selectors are not supported yet. Multiline comments and other HTML
comments are left alone.

Skillful 2 bodies do not support tokens or legacy brace fences. Skillful 1 keeps
its original markup. Dependencies use the consuming project's body syntax, so
select a pin whose bodies already use comment fences.
`skillful schema` lists harness facts and the project's markup.

Skillful 2 also rejects legacy brace markup in frontmatter. For agent-specific
skill frontmatter, set `<skill>.<field> on <agent> = "value"` in `skill.mod`.

```bash
skillful fmt --check
skillful check --strict
skillful inspect <skill> --rendered
```

`skillful author` is not a command.

# core

Author skills, commands, and rules once. Skillful renders that one corpus for each
harness: `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `grok`, `opencode`, `pi`. Git is how you pull
other people's skill trees (`github:`, `git:`, `path:`).

Plain files are enough for a single harness. Use skillful when one tree must serve
several harnesses, or when you compose another tree with your own.

You pick the command and the targets. If a verb or topic is unknown, read
`skills tree` or `<command> -h` and retry. Do not invent commands. A verb that is
not in `-h` does not exist. Flags live on `skillful <command> -h`.

Only `add` and `update` resolve revisions. `add` also fetches. `fetch` retrieves
exact existing pins. Inspection, check, render, install, and historical diff never
resolve or contact the network. Only `install` writes live harness destinations.

```bash
skillful skills tree
skillful list skills
skillful list setups
skillful inspect <skill>
skillful render --dry-run
skillful install work-mac --dry-run
```

Unclear what a command is for → `skillful skills show <topic>` with a name from the tree.

# deps

Pull other skill trees with Git. `add` declares, resolves, locks, and fetches one
tree. `update name` creates or moves that declaration's pin without requiring
unrelated pins; bare `update` reconciles every remote declaration atomically.
In skillful 2, bare `update` checks `use` selections before writing the lock.
`fetch` retrieves selected or all exact pins and never rewrites `skill.lock`.

Not `inspect` (that reads what you already have). Not `mod` (that declares the require).

```bash
skillful add agent-browser
skillful add github:owner/repo
skillful fetch agent-browser
skillful update agent-browser
```

New GitHub refs default to `@HEAD`, the repository's default branch. In skillful 1,
`add` infers a name from the repository or subdirectory without `--name`. Omit
`--only` / `--exclude` to include the whole tree. Explicit details must match an
existing declaration.

In skillful 2, a `use` declaration is identified by its exact ref, such as
`skillful update github:angular/skills@main`. `fetch` and `update` can reuse pins
from a skillful 1 lock with matching refs. A named update replaces the old pin
when it can match a changed ref unambiguously to the same source. To add a new
`use`, pass `--only` for each skill; `add` refuses a conflicting ref for an
existing source.
`skillful update` and `skillful add` record baselines for new `=` overrides from
the prior pin if there is one, so `skillful check` can report upstream drift.

`path:` dependencies are live source and stay out of `skill.lock`. Paths resolve
from `skill.mod`; a nested project may use a sibling within the same Git source
workspace, such as `path:../shared/skills`.
Inspection, check, render, and install never resolve or fetch. A missing cache
points to `skillful fetch`.

`skillful deps` is not a command. Flags: `skillful add -h`, `skillful update -h`.

# inspect

Read-only evidence: list what the project delivers, explain one skill, validate,
or diff. Never writes, never resolves, never fetches.

Not `render` (that writes a build tree).

```bash
skillful list skills
skillful inspect <skill>
skillful inspect <skill> --rendered
skillful check --strict
skillful diff <skill>
```

`inspect` without `--rendered` is the authored view. `--rendered` is per harness.
Pass a built-in or top-level declared agent to `inspect --harness`. When an agent's
skills path is set only on machines, `check` uses those machine configurations.

If `check` reports drift for an `=` override, review the upstream change before
accepting it. `skillful update` alone keeps the existing baseline. Temporarily
remove the affected override from `skill.mod` and run `skillful update` with no
arguments to drop its baseline. Restore the override and run `skillful update`
again to record a new baseline, then verify with `skillful check --strict`.

`diff --against REV` materializes only a revision already in the local Git object
database.

`skillful inspect -h`

# mod

`skill.mod` is the project declaration. `fmt` parses and rewrites it. Every mutating
command uses the same formatter.

Not `deps` (that resolves and fetches what this file declares).

The first directive is `skillful 1` or `skillful 2`. `fmt` keeps that version.

Use `skillful migrate` (or `skillful migrate --project ./agent`) to rewrite a
skillful 1 manifest in place. Migration keeps the revisions of selected sources,
merges duplicate pins at the same revision, and removes unused pins. Run
`skillful fetch` first if a pin is missing from the cache. Migration stops rather
than guessing at settings with no direct translation, such as custom tokens or
setups with different agent lists. If it cannot find an omitted skill, declare
its source or remove the omission if the skill is retired.
Migration also rewrites legacy body fences in local skills, commands, and rules.
Remove brace markup from frontmatter and write literal values in place of tokens.
Run `skillful migrate`, then add `<skill>.<field> on <agent> = "value"` in the
skillful 2 `skill.mod` if needed. Migration refuses body tokens outside code and
legacy fences that skillful 2 would treat as code.
It does not rewrite dependencies: select a compatible pin if an imported body
still uses legacy fences.
Setup install path overrides become `harness` paths inside the corresponding
`machine`, except that `.agents/skills` overrides for agents that read the shared
folder use shared placement instead. Run `skillful render <machine>` afterward
to verify the delivered files.

```text
skillful 2

local ./skills ./commands
rules ./rules/global_agents.md

use github:angular/skills@main { angular-developer angular-new-app }

agents claude pi codex

only angular-developer on pi "Uses Pi tools."

skip angular-new-app on codex "Only scaffold in Claude Code and Pi."

machine work-mac
machine personal skip angular-developer angular-new-app
```

`local` takes the skill root, then the command root. Without `local` or `rules`,
Skillful uses `./skills`, `./commands`, and `./rules/global_agents.md` if present
and skips any that are missing. Explicit paths must exist. `use` names the exact
skills from a `github:`, `git:`, or `path:` source. Each declared agent gets every
selected skill unless it is skipped for that agent or machine, or restricted by
`only <skills> on <agents> "reason"`. An `only` line limits delivery to the named
agents without adding them to the machine. Multiple `only` lines for the same
skill combine their agent lists; `skip` still excludes a skill.
Unknown directives, agents, or skill names are errors with a line number; skill
names are checked when resolving sources (`check` or `render`), not during `fmt`.

Use `harness` to change install paths, or define an agent and list it in `agents`:

```text
agents claude pi local-agent
harness pi { rules .pi/agent/GENERAL.md }
harness local-agent {
  skills .local-agent/skills
  commands .local-agent/commands
  rules .local-agent/RULES.md
  reads-shared
}
machine laptop
machine work-mac {
  harness pi { rules .pi/agent/WORK.md }
  skip angular-new-app
}
```

Paths are relative to the install root (your home by default). A machine's
fields win over top-level fields; unset fields keep their defaults. A new agent
needs a `skills` path. Set `commands` to install separate command files;
otherwise an agent without a command destination gets commands as skills.
`reads-shared` opts an agent into `.agents/skills`. Claude Code defaults to
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`; Cursor has no default rules path.
Replace a skill's front-matter field with `<skill>.<field> = "…"`, or add text
with `<skill>.<field>.append = "…"`. Use an unquoted project-relative file path
instead of a quoted string to read the value from a file. For one agent, put
`on <agent>` before `=`:

```text
angular-developer.description = "Angular guidance"
angular-developer.description.append on pi = " Use the process tool for builds."
```

Use `.body =` to replace the instructions or `.body.append =` to add text
verbatim (include a leading newline if needed). Use `.body.replace` to swap an
exact passage. Both operands can be quoted values or project-relative paths.
Rendering stops if the passage does not appear exactly once.
Body overrides are applied before fences are evaluated.

```text
angular-developer.body = ./overlays/angular-developer-full.md
angular-developer.body.append on pi = """

  Run `ng build` through the process tool.

  """
ketchup.body.replace """
  Draw a Mermaid diagram of the flow.
  """ with """
  <!-- only claude -->
  Describe the flow as a numbered list.
  <!-- end -->
  <!-- skip claude -->
  Draw a Mermaid sequence diagram of the flow.
  <!-- end -->
  """
```

Use `"""` anywhere skillful 2 accepts a quoted value. The opener ends its line;
start the closer on a new line. The directive can continue after the closer.
Indent each nonempty content line with the same spaces or tabs as the closer;
that prefix is stripped, and extra indentation is kept. Text is literal (no
escapes), and the newlines next to the delimiters are not part of the value.
Add a blank content line to include a leading or trailing newline.

`skillful fmt` writes multiline values as blocks and single-line literals as
JSON strings. It keeps JSON quoting if a value contains a carriage return or a
line that would be read as the closing delimiter. HTML-comment fences in override
bodies are evaluated per agent, just like fences in the original body.
Every-agent overrides run first, then agent-specific ones, each in file order.
The agent's existing front-matter rules still apply. Overrides require a skill
selected by the project. Run `skillful update` to record the upstream fields and
bodies replaced by `=` in `skill.lock`; `skillful check` warns if those drift.
Appends and exact-passage replacements do not get drift warnings.

Skillful 1 keeps `skills`, `commands`, and `rules` roots, `require` with `only` or
`exclude`, and `harness` and `setup` blocks. Source paths stay inside their allowed
roots in both versions.

`init` writes a skillful 2 project with local examples and an `example` machine.
Render it or preview an install before making any edits:

```bash
skillful init --dir ./agent
cd ./agent
skillful render
skillful install example --dry-run
skillful fmt --check
skillful fmt
skillful check
```

`skillful mod` is not a command. For pins, run `skillful skills show deps`.

# render

Render a managed build tree. By default, render uses the agents in skillful 2 or
the declared harnesses in skillful 1. Name a machine or setup to apply its skill
selection. In skillful 2, a skill goes in `.agents/skills` only when at least two
shared-folder agents (Codex, Grok, Pi, OpenCode, or Cursor) get the same copy.
Skills for a lone reader, or skills that differ or are skipped, use the receiving
agents' own folders. Claude Code always uses `.claude/skills`. Skillful 1 continues
to render skills in `<harness>/skills`.

`--harness` refreshes the named outputs. Select a built-in or top-level declared
agent. In skillful 2 it can also regroup already-rendered skills in the same
machine layout and refresh their contracts without touching commands or rules.
If a partial render would remove a skill a retained agent still uses, run a full
render without `--harness`, naming the machine if applicable.
Only `install` writes live harness destinations. `--dry-run` first.

Not `inspect` (that does not write). Not a substitute for editing sources.

```bash
skillful render --dry-run
skillful render work-mac
skillful render --harness pi --out ./rendered
skillful install work-mac --dry-run
skillful install --harness opencode --path skills=.config/opencode-v2/skills --path commands=.config/opencode-v2/commands
```

`install` records exclusive ownership, refuses unmanaged or edited collisions,
and removes only unchanged stale files. Different destination roots stay
independent. `--path` installs one public harness into a nonstandard layout. An
OpenCode install at retired `opencode-v2` paths adopts that receipt and migrates
unchanged stale files. `--force` never permits an escape, takes files through
another path, receipt, or symlink alias, or deletes a changed stale file.
A skillful 2 machine install takes over earlier one-agent installs for its agents
from the same project and destination root. It refuses to install a private copy
for a shared-folder agent if another installation owns that skill in `.agents/skills`.
It also refuses to publish a shared copy if another installation in the same
root owns a private copy in a shared reader's skills path.
`--harness` on install is skillful 1 only.
After an interrupted install, follow the lock recovery instructions and rerun `install`.
`install <setup> --remove` rejects `--force` and retires only unchanged files
from that setup's receipt. A named render contains only that setup's selected
skills and harness outputs.

`skillful render -h` · `skillful install -h`

# setup

In skillful 2, `skillful install` selects the machine matching your lowercase
short hostname. If none matches, it lists the declared machines. To select one
explicitly, run `skillful install personal`. `machine personal skip
company-database` uses the listed `agents` and skips that skill for all of them.
Preview the machine with `render personal` or `setup show personal`.
`setup show` lists rules paths only when the machine installs rules.

Skillful 1 uses setup blocks for skill selection, harness outputs, root kind,
and path exceptions:

```text
setup personal (
  omit-skill company-database "Work only."
  pi claude
)

setup work-mac (
  pi

  claude (
    skills .claude2/skills
  )
)
```

Omit `root` to use each harness's home paths. `root project` selects its project
paths; `--root DIR` relocates the selected profile when applying. Bare harness
names use those conventional paths. A harness block contains only exceptions.

Skillful 2 machine installs use `.agents/skills` only when at least two listed
shared-folder agents get the same copy. Skills for a lone reader, or skills that
differ or are skipped, go into the receiving agents' own folders. Claude Code
always uses `.claude/skills`. Skillful 1 setups keep their existing harness paths.

Codex, Cursor, Grok, and OpenCode project profiles do not claim `AGENTS.md`.
Assign `rules AGENTS.md` explicitly to one harness when the project needs it.
Only skillful 1 supports one-off `install --harness`. It uses home paths, with
`--root` as relocation.

Use repeated `only-skill <name>` or repeated `omit-skill <name> <reason>`, never
both. Selection names are exact. Omitting a skill also removes its support files
from every output in the setup. Omit a command with `omit-command` in a harness block.

```bash
skillful list setups
skillful setup show work-mac
skillful render work-mac
skillful install work-mac --dry-run
skillful install work-mac
skillful install old-work --remove --dry-run
skillful install old-work --remove
```

`render` is a managed build tree. Only `install` writes live destinations.
Use `install <name> --remove` to retire an instance from its ownership receipt.
After deleting its declaration, pass the exact original `--root`. Valid source
overrides are ignored during removal; destinations come only from the receipt.
Removal rejects `--force` and deletes only unchanged owned files.

`skillful skills show mod` · `skillful skills show render`
